messages.text:
Hello! I'm interested in your material section and have a couple of questions
 

 For the batting, what is "I get 30%"?
 Photo attached - this is in the material section.
 

 And for the silk, would the fluff be similar to down? For example, if I wanted to make a down jacket or mitts, can I use this as a fill?
 Or if I make a quilted fabric with panels, I will want to fill it with down our silk fluff to make it warm and light. 
 

 

 Thank you and kindest regards,
 Aki

messages.subject: Re:
messages.text:
Hello Aki,
 

 Thank you for your thoughtful questions 😊
 

 Regarding the “30%” mention, this is most likely a translation error on the website. When purchasing our loose fiber, it is 100% pure milkweed fiber , sourced from Canada.
 

 The 30% reference may apply to certain finished textile products that contain fiber blends, but the bulk fiber itself is entirely milkweed.
 As for your second question: in terms of thermal performance, milkweed silk (floss) offers insulation comparable to down. It can absolutely be used as a filling for jackets, mittens, or quilted panels.
 

 However, based on our experience, we generally recommend blending the fiber rather than using 100% pure milkweed on its own. In our early products, we used only pure milkweed fiber and found that it tended to compress and shift more quickly over time.
 

 To improve durability and performance, we introduced two adjustments:
 Adding a quilting step to stabilize the fiber;

 Blending milkweed fiber with polyester to provide more structure and resilience.

 

 This blend improves long-term durability, reduces compression, and limits fiber migration inside the product.
 

 For a project like a jacket or quilted panels, we would strongly recommend either blending the fiber or designing well-structured compartments to maintain loft and insulation performance over time.
 

 If you have any other questions, please don’t hesitate to let us know.
 

 Warm regards,
 __
 Laurence 
 

 Lasclay
